routing_balance_normalization: mean over depth calls per block, then mean over blocks

depth_dist/step_.population: every token of every training batch, all recursion steps
depth_dist/step_.note: Accumulated in the training loop, so it includes tokens that hit the max-depth forced exit -- step_7_pct matches halt/forced_exit_rate exactly. NOT comparable with depth/hist, which is the validation pass.

depth/hist/step_.population: every position except each block's last, which has no next-token target and therefore no per-token loss
depth/hist/step_.note: The token-level exit-depth histogram over the whole validation split. Counts, not percentages, and over a different pass and population than depth_dist/*, so the two will not agree.

depth/mean_by_family/.population: positions with a mapped POS family (-1 excluded), last position of each block excluded
depth/mean_by_family/.note: Companion to depth/hist. Differs from recursion/avg_depth_by_family in the fifth decimal precisely because that one includes each block's last position.

recursion/avg_depth_by_family/.population: positions with step_mask true and a mapped oracle family, INCLUDING each block's last position
recursion/avg_depth_by_family/.note: The pre-existing arithmetic key, kept unchanged because Gate L0 checks the contract it belongs to. The last-position difference is the whole of its disagreement with depth/mean_by_family.

recursion/avg_depth_by_op/.population: positions with a mapped operation code
recursion/avg_depth_by_op/.note: Arithmetic only. Empty on language, because lang_families.ALL_OP_NAMES is [] -- there is no operation axis. On opdiff the axis is the OPERATION INSTANCE: one entry per (operation, k), so the F rows carry one entry per iteration count.

ood_interp/avg_depth_by_op/.population: positions with step_mask true and a valid operation-INSTANCE axis entry
ood_interp/avg_depth_by_op/.note: T-OD.3. The per-iteration-count average exit depth on the HELD-OUT INTERPOLATION split (k = 3, 6, 9, 11, 14 -- inside the trained range, none of them trained). The compute-versus-k claim is read off this table and its ood_extrap/ twin: the question is whether the depth GROWS with k on iteration counts the model has never seen, and the two splits answer two different questions about it.

ood_extrap/avg_depth_by_op/.population: positions with step_mask true and a valid operation-INSTANCE axis entry
ood_extrap/avg_depth_by_op/.note: T-OD.3. The same table on the EXTRAPOLATION split (k = 17, 20 -- beyond the trained range). A stretch result: the high bit appeared only alone in training, so this is reported as a stretch and not as an expectation.

depth/spearman_.population: the same positions as depth/hist, so all three correlations are over one identical token set (T-L6.1)
depth/spearman_.note: Each carries its own permutation null band. At n ~ 2.8e5 the band is about +-0.004, so exceeds_null says almost nothing about EFFECT SIZE -- read it with depth/std and depth/hist or not at all.

depth/by_document/.population: all positions except each block's last, grouped by document via the count of eot_id tokens before each position
depth/by_document/.note: T-L6.7's within- vs between-document variance decomposition. `total`, `within` and `between` are token-weighted POPULATION variances and sum exactly, which `sum_matches_total` reports rather than assumes. `between_share` is the passage-level allocation number; per-document means are summarised (std/min/max) rather than logged one key each.

depth/embed_norm_.population: the same positions as depth/hist; the norm is per TYPE and is gathered by token id, read at THIS epoch
depth/embed_norm_.note: T-L6.10's confound diagnostics. `logfreq_partial_norm` is the CORRECTED frequency-depth correlation and the number to quote; `depth_vs_norm` and `logfreq_vs_norm` are the confound's strength, published beside it so the correction is readable. `logfreq_within_bins_*` is a secondary assumption-free cross-check that UNDER-corrects (see spearman_within_bins), so a low value from it is informative and a high one is not conclusive.

depth/allocation_error_.note: Structurally undefined on language: there is no per-token ground-truth depth for English (plan_language.md §5.1), so the value is the string N/A. A 0.0 here would read as perfect allocation against a curriculum that does not exist.

routing_agreement_caption: AGREEMENT WITH A GROUP PRIOR, NOT ACCURACY. mean(predicted_expert == row_group) against the generator's designed partition of the 25 operations into seven expert groups (E1 BITWISE, E2 SHIFT/MINMAX, E3 ADD/SUB, E4 MUL, E5 DIV/MOD, E6 SORT/MEDIAN, E7 ITER/GCD). The partition is a PRIOR, not a functional ground truth: a router that separates SHL from REV may be the better partition of the operation space while scoring low here. Read the permutation-invariant metrics first -- Hungarian accuracy, AMI and purity -- and read the load entropy against this task's own group marginals. The group label is NEVER an input feature: the model sees only token ids, and it has to infer the operation from the operation token in the sequence.

routing_permutation_invariant.note: expert indices carry no semantic identity; read the gap between raw_accuracy and hungarian_accuracy, not either alone (updated_rules.md 8.3). per_family is under the IDENTITY mapping and is only interpretable when step_routing supervised the index; per_family_matched applies hungarian_assignment first and is the table to report for an unsupervised router (T6.8).
